title: Geometric and quotient data for a flat blowup square
statement: Let $f:X\to S$, $e:T\to S$, $g:Y\to T$, $j:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $fj=eg$, and assume $e$ and $j$ flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_S$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], put $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}S\to S$ and $b_T:B_T=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_T}T\to T$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-extended-ideal], and let $\operatorname{bc}_e:B_T\to T\times_SB$ be the specified comparison [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]. Put $\beta=\operatorname{pr}_B\operatorname{bc}_e$, $P=X\times_SB$, $Q=Y\times_TB_T$, with projections $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to B$, $r:Q\to Y$, $s:Q\to B_T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $D=q^{-1}b^{-1}V(\mathcal I)$ and $D_Q=s^{-1}b_T^{-1}V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_T)$, regarding these as closed subsets. Then the pair $(jr,\beta s)$ defines a morphism $u:Q\to P$ with $pu=jr$. The comparison $\operatorname{bc}_e$ is an isomorphism over $T$, and there is a canonical isomorphism $Q\cong Y\times_XP$ with projections $r,u$. The morphism $u$ is flat, and $D_Q=u^{-1}D$. Every point of $P$ has an affine neighbourhood $V$ and $a\in\mathcal O_P(V)$ with $D\cap V=V(a)$; on any affine $W\subseteq u^{-1}V$, $D_Q\cap W=V(a_W)$, where $a_W$ is the image of $a$. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], put $H=p^*\mathcal F$ and $H_Q=r^*j^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Define submodule sheaves $K\subseteq H$ and $K_Q\subseteq H_Q$ by $K(V)=\{h\in H(V):h|_{V\setminus D}=0\}$ and $K_Q(W)=\{h\in H_Q(W):h|_{W\setminus D_Q}=0\}$ for every open $V\subseteq P$, $W\subseteq Q$. These four sheaves are quasi-coherent. The two module strict transforms [def-trf-module-strict-transform] have quotient presentations $\mathcal F^B=H/K$ and $(j^*\mathcal F)^{B_T}=H_Q/K_Q$, with their defining quotient maps $\pi$ and $\pi_Q$. The identity $pu=jr$ and the composition isomorphisms for module pullback give the canonical isomorphism $\gamma:u^*H\xrightarrow{\sim}H_Q$.

proof.text: By [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change], the specified $\operatorname{bc}_e$ of [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map] is an isomorphism over $T$; hence $b\beta=eb_T$. Using $fj=eg$ and $gr=b_Ts$ gives $f(jr)=egr=eb_Ts=b(\beta s)$. The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore defines $u=(jr,\beta s):Q\to P$ with $pu=jr$ and $qu=\beta s$.

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up; the specified comparison followed by the fibre-product universal property.

proof.text: The maps $(r,u)$ define $\phi:Q\to Y\times_XP$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. To construct its inverse, take any test scheme $R$ with maps $y:R\to Y$, $z:R\to P$ satisfying $jy=pz$. Then $egy=fjy=fpz=bqz$, so $(gy,qz)$ defines $R\to T\times_SB$. Composing with $\operatorname{bc}_e^{-1}$ gives $t:R\to B_T$ with $b_Tt=gy$ and $\beta t=qz$. Thus $(y,t)$ defines $R\to Q$. In the two composites the $Y,B_T$ projections, respectively the $Y,P$ projections, agree with the original ones; uniqueness in the fibre-product property makes both composites identities. This is the required canonical isomorphism, identifying $u$ with the projection to $P$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], that projection is flat, being the base change of the assumed flat $j$ along $p$. The isomorphism identifies the local ring maps, so $u$ is flat by [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0805, lemma-flat-base-change-blowing-up, cartesian square; morphisms.tex Tag 01U9, lemma-base-change-flat. The reassociation is written out by the universal property.

proof.text: By [def-nagata-extended-ideal], $V(\mathcal I\mathcal O_T)$ is the inverse-image closed subscheme $T\times_SV(\mathcal I)$. Locally, a ring map $A\to C$ and an ideal $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ give the pushout $C\otimes_A A/I=C/(a_1,\ldots,a_n)C$: a map out of either side is exactly a map out of $C$ killing all the $a_i$. Thus its underlying closed set is $e^{-1}V(I)$, since a prime of $C$ contains the images of $I$ exactly when its contraction contains $I$. This also verifies finite type of the extended ideal, using the images of the same finite local generators [pqf-def-coherent]. Consequently $D_Q=(b_Ts)^{-1}e^{-1}V(\mathcal I)=(b\beta s)^{-1}V(\mathcal I)=(bqu)^{-1}V(\mathcal I)=u^{-1}D$.

source.place: Tag 01JV, definition-inverse-image-closed-subscheme; affine quotient-ring universal property and inverse images of closed sets.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] first to $p$ and $\mathcal F$, then to $j$ and $\mathcal F$, and then to $r$ and $j^*\mathcal F$. This gives quasi-coherence of $H=p^*\mathcal F$ and $H_Q=r^*j^*\mathcal F$; none of these applications requires flatness.

Put $E=b^{-1}V(\mathcal I)\subseteq B$. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], its ideal is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor, so $E$ is locally principal. Apply [lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel] to $(q:P\to B,E,H)$ and $(qu:Q\to B,E,H_Q)$. Step 3 identifies the second inverse image with $D_Q$; the sectionwise kernels in that lemma are exactly $K$ and $K_Q$. Both are therefore quasi-coherent. The same lemma makes $D$ locally principal. Shrink a neighbourhood of any point of $P$ to an affine $V$ on which its ideal is generated by $a\in\mathcal O_P(V)$; then $D\cap V=V(a)$. For any affine $W\subseteq u^{-1}V$, the ring map $\mathcal O_P(V)\to\mathcal O_Q(W)$ takes $a$ to $a_W$. By the prime-ideal test in Step 3, the preimage of $V(a)$ in $W$ is $V(a_W)$, which equals $D_Q\cap W$. No nonzerodivisor assertion is made for $a$ or $a_W$.

source.place: Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor; Tag 053P, lemma-pullback-locally-principal; paragraph before Tag 080D. Supported-kernel quasi-coherence: properties.tex Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset.

proof.text: By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], the strict transform for $(f,\mathcal I,\mathcal F)$ is $H$ modulo sections vanishing off $D$, namely $H/K$, and its defining map is the quotient $\pi$. Applying the same definition to $(g,\mathcal I\mathcal O_T,j^*\mathcal F)$ gives $H_Q/K_Q$ and $\pi_Q$. Here the extended centre is finite type by Step 3 and $j^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by Step 4. Finally the composition isomorphisms explicitly supplied in [def-pc-module-pullback], evaluated at $\mathcal F$ and the equality $pu=jr$ from Step 1, give $\gamma:u^*H=u^*p^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}(pu)^*\mathcal F=(jr)^*\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}r^*j^*\mathcal F=H_Q$. These are the asserted ordinary-pullback and quotient data.
